entries.what: Model claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (Claude Sonnet 4) is retired, so requests to it fail. The Sonnet 5.5 guide says it stays available on Google-managed Vertex and Bedrock. Alias forms claude-sonnet-4-0 and claude-sonnet-4 are a reading: the retirement page lists only the dated id. The date applies to Anthropic-operated platforms. Amazon Bedrock and Google-managed Vertex set their own schedules, so their ids (anthropic.claude-...-v1:0, claude-...@date) are not covered by this entry.
entries.replacement: claude-sonnet-5-5, as the page lists it. Active, retirement not sooner than September 28, 2027.
requires: Moving to claude-sonnet-5-5 changes more than the name. Full list: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide.
Thinking runs by default: a request with no thinking field now runs adaptive thinking, where the old model ran without it.

A reply can start with thinking blocks, so code reading response.content[0].text breaks. Read blocks by type and take the ones whose type is text. The same goes for a stream handler that treats the first block as text: the Opus 5.5 guide says so, and this guide does not.

Code that returns response.content as a string, or passes it on whole, now carries thinking blocks with the text. Pull out the text blocks first. (A reading of the same rule: the page names content[0].text.)

max_tokens covers thinking plus text, and thinking tokens bill as output, so revisit small values such as a classifier or title call. A small limit can stop with stop_reason max_tokens before any text: the Haiku 5.5 guide says this outright, and for Sonnet 5.5 it is a reading of the same rule. The thinking cost page adds that a limit sized for no thinking is often too small. Raise it, lower the effort, or send thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} at high effort or below.
thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N} returns a 400. Remove the budget and set output_config.effort. There is no fixed mapping from a budget to a level.

thinking: {"type": "disabled"} returns a 400. To run without up-front thinking send {"type": "between_tools"}, which takes no other field and returns a 400 at xhigh or max effort. With it, a per-message output_config.effort that differs from the level in effect also returns a 400.

temperature, top_p and top_k return a 400 at a non-default value, and always under API version 2026-10-21 (AN-2). The top_p default is 0.99, so top_p: 1 returns a 400, and so does sending temperature and top_p together, even at defaults. Remove them on the Anthropic path, even if a shared config still holds them for other providers.

tool_choice of type any or tool returns a 400, including on token counting. Send {"type": "auto"}, mark the tool strict: true with additionalProperties: false on every object, and say in the prompt when to use it, because the model can now answer without calling the tool. A request can have at most 20 strict tools. Strict mode takes a subset of JSON Schema, and MCP, computer use and browser use toolset entries do not accept strict. Structured outputs is the other route to schema-valid output.

Pass thinking blocks back unchanged in tool-use loops, including empty ones. Edited, reordered or partly dropped blocks in the latest assistant turn return a 400, so echo the turn rather than rebuilding it.

Keep conversations append-only. Replaying a block after editing the system prompt, tools or an earlier message returns a 400 on accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, when thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior is unset. Older accounts get it only with that field set to "error". Setting it to "drop_block" with the thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 header drops the blocks instead, and block_binding works only with thinking type adaptive.

Sonnet 5.5 thinking blocks work only in the account that produced them or one linked to it. From another account they are dropped and the request still succeeds, so replay stored conversations through the same account.

Thinking blocks from earlier turns now stay in context and count as input, where Sonnet 4.5 and earlier keep only the last turn. Long conversations carry more input tokens. Thinking block clearing removes them.
Thinking text is omitted by default: blocks arrive with an empty thinking field. Set display: "summarized" if the app shows it.

Notes longer than a sentence or two between tool calls now come back as thinking blocks, empty at the default display, so an interface that shows them goes quiet. No request fails. To get them, set display to "updates" (beta, thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 header) or "summarized", or use between_tools, and render each non-empty block before the tool_use block after it.

Computer use needs the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset: computer_20250124 is rejected on every platform, and computer_20251124 is rejected on the Claude API. Bedrock also accepts computer_20251124 with the computer-use-2025-11-24 header. Drop the old version's beta header when moving, and fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14 too, because it returns a 400 alongside a toolset entry. The agent loop changes as well: handle every member tool_use block in a turn, echo toolset_name on results, and read the action from the block's name, not input.action.
The advisor tool accepts fewer advisors: Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 5.5 advisors return a 400, and the advice comes back encrypted as an advisor_redacted_result block.

Handle stop_reason refusal, which arrives as an HTTP 200. Sonnet 5.5 declines in more categories than Sonnet 5, named in stop_details: cyber, bio, frontier_llm, reasoning_extraction and general_harms. Server-side fallback retries only cyber and frontier_llm. Real-time cyber safeguards are new for code from Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5.

The same text counts about 30 percent more tokens than on Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5 (the page gives no figure for older models), and a large image can cost up to 4,784 tokens. Recount, and revisit max_tokens and cost.
The minimum cacheable prompt drops to 512 tokens from 1,024 on Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5, so prompts too short to cache before can now create cache entries. No code change is needed.

A prefilled last assistant turn returns a 400: the conversation must end with a user message. For output format use structured outputs or tools with enum fields; move preambles to the system prompt, and continuations and context reminders to the user turn.
Parse tool call input with a standard JSON parser, because escaping can differ.

Set output_config.effort explicitly, as the guide says for Sonnet 4.5 or earlier: Sonnet 4.5 has no effort parameter. The default on the Claude API is high, and the levels are recalibrated, so run an effort sweep rather than carrying a setting over.
Remove any context-window beta header and interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14. Replace fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14 with eager_input_streaming: true on each tool that needs it.

Move output_format to output_config.format: output_format returns a 400 without the structured-outputs-2025-11-13 beta header. The Opus 5.5 guide adds that Python SDK v1.0 and later does not accept output_format on client.beta.messages.create() or count_tokens(). The parse() and stream() helpers keep it.
Use text_editor_20250728 with the tool name str_replace_based_edit_tool and no undo_edit command, and code_execution_20260521.

Handle the model_context_window_exceeded stop reason. Claude 4.5 and later accept a request whose input plus max_tokens exceeds the window and stop with this reason. Earlier models returned a validation error.
Tool call string parameters keep their trailing newlines, so check exact string matches.
Remove the token-efficient-tools-2025-02-19 and output-128k-2025-02-19 beta headers.
Review prompts: Claude 4 and later models are more concise and need explicit direction.

Amazon Bedrock and Google-managed Vertex set their own schedules, so their ids (anthropic.claude-...-v1:0, claude-...@date) are not covered by this entry.
future.replacement: claude-sonnet-5-5, as the page lists it. Active, retirement not sooner than September 28, 2027.
requires: Moving to claude-sonnet-5-5 changes more than the name. Full list: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide.
Thinking runs by default: a request with no thinking field now runs adaptive thinking, where the old model ran without it.

A reply can start with thinking blocks, so code reading response.content[0].text breaks. Read blocks by type and take the ones whose type is text. The same goes for a stream handler that treats the first block as text: the Opus 5.5 guide says so, and this guide does not.

Code that returns response.content as a string, or passes it on whole, now carries thinking blocks with the text. Pull out the text blocks first. (A reading of the same rule: the page names content[0].text.)

max_tokens covers thinking plus text, and thinking tokens bill as output, so revisit small values such as a classifier or title call. A small limit can stop with stop_reason max_tokens before any text: the Haiku 5.5 guide says this outright, and for Sonnet 5.5 it is a reading of the same rule. The thinking cost page adds that a limit sized for no thinking is often too small. Raise it, lower the effort, or send thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} at high effort or below.
thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N} returns a 400. Remove the budget and set output_config.effort. There is no fixed mapping from a budget to a level.

thinking: {"type": "disabled"} returns a 400. To run without up-front thinking send {"type": "between_tools"}, which takes no other field and returns a 400 at xhigh or max effort. With it, a per-message output_config.effort that differs from the level in effect also returns a 400.

temperature, top_p and top_k return a 400 at a non-default value, and always under API version 2026-10-21 (AN-2). The top_p default is 0.99, so top_p: 1 returns a 400, and so does sending temperature and top_p together, even at defaults. Remove them on the Anthropic path, even if a shared config still holds them for other providers.

tool_choice of type any or tool returns a 400, including on token counting. Send {"type": "auto"}, mark the tool strict: true with additionalProperties: false on every object, and say in the prompt when to use it, because the model can now answer without calling the tool. A request can have at most 20 strict tools. Strict mode takes a subset of JSON Schema, and MCP, computer use and browser use toolset entries do not accept strict. Structured outputs is the other route to schema-valid output.

Pass thinking blocks back unchanged in tool-use loops, including empty ones. Edited, reordered or partly dropped blocks in the latest assistant turn return a 400, so echo the turn rather than rebuilding it.

Keep conversations append-only. Replaying a block after editing the system prompt, tools or an earlier message returns a 400 on accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, when thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior is unset. Older accounts get it only with that field set to "error". Setting it to "drop_block" with the thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 header drops the blocks instead, and block_binding works only with thinking type adaptive.

Sonnet 5.5 thinking blocks work only in the account that produced them or one linked to it. From another account they are dropped and the request still succeeds, so replay stored conversations through the same account.

Thinking blocks from earlier turns now stay in context and count as input, where Sonnet 4.5 and earlier keep only the last turn. Long conversations carry more input tokens. Thinking block clearing removes them.
Thinking text is omitted by default: blocks arrive with an empty thinking field. Set display: "summarized" if the app shows it.

Notes longer than a sentence or two between tool calls now come back as thinking blocks, empty at the default display, so an interface that shows them goes quiet. No request fails. To get them, set display to "updates" (beta, thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 header) or "summarized", or use between_tools, and render each non-empty block before the tool_use block after it.

Computer use needs the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset: computer_20250124 is rejected on every platform, and computer_20251124 is rejected on the Claude API. Bedrock also accepts computer_20251124 with the computer-use-2025-11-24 header. Drop the old version's beta header when moving, and fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14 too, because it returns a 400 alongside a toolset entry. The agent loop changes as well: handle every member tool_use block in a turn, echo toolset_name on results, and read the action from the block's name, not input.action.
The advisor tool accepts fewer advisors: Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 5.5 advisors return a 400, and the advice comes back encrypted as an advisor_redacted_result block.

Handle stop_reason refusal, which arrives as an HTTP 200. Sonnet 5.5 declines in more categories than Sonnet 5, named in stop_details: cyber, bio, frontier_llm, reasoning_extraction and general_harms. Server-side fallback retries only cyber and frontier_llm. Real-time cyber safeguards are new for code from Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5.

The same text counts about 30 percent more tokens than on Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5 (the page gives no figure for older models), and a large image can cost up to 4,784 tokens. Recount, and revisit max_tokens and cost.
The minimum cacheable prompt drops to 512 tokens from 1,024 on Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5, so prompts too short to cache before can now create cache entries. No code change is needed.

A prefilled last assistant turn returns a 400: the conversation must end with a user message. For output format use structured outputs or tools with enum fields; move preambles to the system prompt, and continuations and context reminders to the user turn.
Parse tool call input with a standard JSON parser, because escaping can differ.

Set output_config.effort explicitly, as the guide says for Sonnet 4.5 or earlier: Sonnet 4.5 has no effort parameter. The default on the Claude API is high, and the levels are recalibrated, so run an effort sweep rather than carrying a setting over.
Remove any context-window beta header and interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14. Replace fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14 with eager_input_streaming: true on each tool that needs it.

Move output_format to output_config.format: output_format returns a 400 without the structured-outputs-2025-11-13 beta header. The Opus 5.5 guide adds that Python SDK v1.0 and later does not accept output_format on client.beta.messages.create() or count_tokens(). The parse() and stream() helpers keep it.
